project.name: Pico-ePaper
project.description: MicroPython firmware for Raspberry Pi Pico W with 3.7" ePaper display, featuring weather display, WiFi connectivity, web-based configuration, NTP time sync, and mDNS service discovery.

nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: Central application controller that manages device lifecycle states (AP mode, STA connection, init, run), wires up WiFi, NTP, weather, scheduler, and display subsystems, and drives the async event loop on the Pico W.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses MicroPython asyncio for cooperative multitasking on RP2040 — no threading, all concurrency via async/await and an event loop.

nodes.name: App
nodes.summary: Main application class that orchestrates device boot, WiFi negotiation, NTP sync, weather fetching, scheduler callbacks, and ePaper display rendering across its full lifecycle.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package initializer that marks the display directory as a MicroPython module package.

nodes.name: canvas.py
nodes.summary: Provides the LandscapeCanvas class that wraps the 3.7" ePaper framebuffer, handling coordinate transposition (portrait hardware rendered as landscape), partial and full display commits, and PBM image blitting.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses MicroPython's framebuf module and includes a viper-accelerated transposition path for performance on the RP2040.

nodes.name: LandscapeCanvas
nodes.summary: Framebuffer subclass that presents a landscape coordinate system over the physically portrait 3.7" ePaper panel, with full and partial refresh commit methods and PBM sprite blitting support.

nodes.name: fonts.py
nodes.summary: Defines and lazy-loads bitmap font modules used across all display screens, with a graceful fallback helper for missing optional fonts.

nodes.name: icons.py
nodes.summary: Loads PBM monochrome bitmap icons from the filesystem into framebuffer objects, with an LRU cache and a path-existence helper used by screen renderers for weather and WiFi icons.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements a small manual LRU cache (list-based) to limit RAM usage on the memory-constrained RP2040.

nodes.name: load_pbm
nodes.summary: Reads a PBM file from the Pico filesystem, converts it into a MicroPython FrameBuffer object, and caches the result with LRU eviction.

nodes.name: exists
nodes.summary: Checks whether a PBM file path exists in the Pico filesystem by listing the parent directory, used as a guard before loading icons.

nodes.name: calendar.py
nodes.summary: Renders a monthly calendar grid onto a canvas region, computing day-of-week layout and highlighting today's date, with support for configurable week-start day and proportional font rendering.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Draws a full monthly calendar grid into a bounded canvas area, placing day-of-week headers and date cells with today's date highlighted via an inverse fill rectangle.

nodes.name: guide.py
nodes.summary: Renders the WiFi setup guide screen that shows AP SSID, password, and configuration URL when the device is in access-point mode awaiting initial setup.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: Clears the canvas and renders centered WiFi connection instructions (SSID, password, config URL) onto the ePaper display for the first-run AP setup flow.

nodes.name: main_screen.py
nodes.summary: Composites the main ePaper display layout showing time, weather data, WiFi signal strength, and a monthly calendar, with separate partial-refresh render functions for time-only and calendar-only updates.

nodes.name: render_full
nodes.summary: Reads current RTC time and config settings, clears the canvas, draws all main-screen widgets (WiFi, time, weather, calendar), and commits a full ePaper refresh.

nodes.name: render_time
nodes.summary: Reads current RTC time and redraws only the time widget using a partial ePaper refresh, minimizing display wear.

nodes.name: render_calendar
nodes.summary: Reads current date from RTC and redraws only the calendar widget using a partial ePaper refresh.

nodes.name: _draw_weather
nodes.summary: Draws the weather panel including condition icon, temperature, description text, and humidity/wind data onto a canvas region, with fallback text rendering when icon files are missing.

nodes.name: _draw_time
nodes.summary: Renders the large time display with configurable 12h/24h format and AM/PM label onto a canvas region, using proportional font sizing and centering.

nodes.name: message.py
nodes.summary: Renders a single centered status message string to the full ePaper screen, used to display loading, error, and progress states during device boot and WiFi operations.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: Clears the canvas, centers the given text string using font metrics, writes it via the font Writer, and commits a full ePaper refresh.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: MicroPython entry point that instantiates the App and runs its async event loop; this is the file MicroPython auto-executes on boot.
nodes.languageNotes: MicroPython automatically executes main.py on device boot after boot.py.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Creates an App instance, runs it via asyncio, and resets the event loop — serves as the top-level boot entry point.

nodes.name: ntp.py
nodes.summary: Provides a sync() function that queries an NTP server, applies a timezone offset, and sets the hardware RTC on the Pico W.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses MicroPython's ntptime module and the machine.RTC class to write the corrected datetime directly to hardware.

nodes.name: sync
nodes.summary: Fetches current time from an NTP host, adjusts for a configurable timezone offset in minutes, and programs the hardware RTC; returns True on success.

nodes.name: scheduler.py
nodes.summary: Provides the Scheduler class, an async time-event dispatcher that fires minute, hour, day, weather-tick, and NTP-tick events based on RTC wall-clock time.

nodes.name: Scheduler
nodes.summary: Async scheduler that polls the RTC at sub-second intervals, fires named time-based events (minute, hour, day, weather, ntp) to registered async handler callbacks, with deduplication to prevent double-firing.

nodes.name: weather.py
nodes.summary: Fetches current weather data from the OpenWeatherMap API, persists results to a rotating log file on the Pico filesystem, and exposes helpers to read and rotate the log.

nodes.name: fetch
nodes.summary: Builds an OpenWeatherMap API URL from config, makes an HTTP GET request with retry logic, parses the JSON response into a weather dict, logs the result, and returns the dict on success or None on failure.

nodes.name: rotate_if_needed
nodes.summary: Checks whether the weather log file has grown beyond one day's worth of entries and rotates it by truncating if needed, preserving only recent data.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package initializer for the third-party mdns_client library; marks the directory as a Python package with no re-exports.

nodes.name: client.py
nodes.summary: Core mDNS client implementation providing the async UDP socket loop, callback management, packet dispatch, address resolution, and question/response sending over the multicast group.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses MicroPython's uasyncio event loop and gc.collect for memory management on the constrained Pico W hardware.

nodes.name: Callback
nodes.summary: Value object representing a registered mDNS response callback with optional timeout and remove-if predicate.

nodes.name: Client
nodes.summary: Async mDNS client managing a UDP multicast socket, routing incoming DNS packets to registered callbacks, and sending outgoing questions and responses.

nodes.name: constants.py
nodes.summary: DNS/mDNS protocol constants including record type codes (A, PTR, SRV, TXT), query class flags, and multicast group address used throughout the library.

nodes.name: parser.py
nodes.summary: DNS packet parser that deserializes raw UDP bytes into structured DNSResponse objects including questions, answers, authorities, and additional records.

nodes.name: parse_packet
nodes.summary: Public entry-point that wraps PacketParser instantiation and parsing, returning a DNSResponse from a raw byte buffer.

nodes.name: PacketParser
nodes.summary: Stateful parser that walks a DNS wire-format byte buffer, decoding compressed names and all record types including SRV, SOA, and MX entries.

nodes.name: responder.py
nodes.summary: mDNS responder that handles incoming DNS questions (PTR, SRV, A, TXT) and sends appropriate resource record answers to advertise registered services on the local network.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses random host postfix generation to avoid name collisions when no explicit hostname is provided.

nodes.name: Responder
nodes.summary: Full mDNS responder that answers PTR/SRV/A/TXT queries for advertised services and manages service advertisement lifecycle.

nodes.name: discovery.py
nodes.summary: mDNS service discovery engine that continuously watches for PTR/SRV/A records, tracks service lifecycles with TTL expiry and refresh, and notifies registered ServiceMonitor observers of additions, updates, and removals.
nodes.languageNotes: Buffers out-of-order A records (IP address responses that arrive before SRV records) and uses gc.collect for memory management on resource-constrained hardware.

nodes.name: ServiceChange
nodes.summary: Value object accumulating added, updated, and removed service sets representing the delta of changes in one discovery tick.

nodes.name: ServiceDiscovery
nodes.summary: Orchestrates continuous mDNS service discovery with TTL-aware expiry, buffered A-record resolution, and observer notification via the ServiceMonitor interface.

nodes.name: service_monitor.py
nodes.summary: Abstract base class defining the ServiceMonitor observer interface with service_added, service_updated, and service_removed callback methods.

nodes.name: ServiceMonitor
nodes.summary: Abstract observer interface that consumers implement to receive service lifecycle callbacks from ServiceDiscovery.

nodes.name: service_response.py
nodes.summary: Data model for a discovered mDNS service instance, holding SRV fields (name, priority, weight, target, port, IPs) with TTL-based expiry, refresh scheduling, and equality semantics.

nodes.name: ServiceResponse
nodes.summary: Represents a discovered network service with TTL tracking, refresh scheduling, and IP address aggregation; implements hash and equality for use in sets.

nodes.name: txt_discovery.py
nodes.summary: TXT record extension of ServiceDiscovery that intercepts TXT DNS records, parses key=value TXT data, and attaches it to corresponding service responses.

nodes.name: TXTServiceDiscovery
nodes.summary: Extends ServiceDiscovery to also parse TXT records and attach their key=value metadata to matched service responses.

nodes.name: structs.py
nodes.summary: Core DNS data structures — DNSQuestion, DNSRecord, DNSResponse, ServiceProtocol, and SRVRecord — with binary serialization (to_bytes) and deserialization methods for wire-format encoding.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses struct.pack/unpack_from for compact binary encoding suitable for memory-constrained MicroPython environments.

nodes.name: DNSQuestion
nodes.summary: Represents a single DNS question with query name and type, providing binary serialization to wire format.

nodes.name: DNSRecord
nodes.summary: Represents a DNS resource record with name, type, class, TTL, and rdata payload, supporting binary serialization and TTL-based invalidation timestamps.

nodes.name: DNSResponse
nodes.summary: Top-level DNS packet structure holding questions, answers, authorities, and additional records with full binary serialization for sending mDNS responses.

nodes.name: ServiceProtocol
nodes.summary: Value object encoding a service protocol triple (protocol, service, domain) and generating the corresponding mDNS service name string.

nodes.name: SRVRecord
nodes.summary: SRV record data structure with priority, weight, port, and target, supporting construction from a raw DNSRecord and binary serialization.

nodes.name: util.py
nodes.summary: Collection of DNS wire-format utility functions for IP/name byte conversion, buffer packing, name parsing, A/TXT record data encoding, and async timeout helpers.

nodes.name: dotted_ip_to_bytes
nodes.summary: Converts a dotted-decimal IPv4 string into a 4-byte bytes object for use in DNS A record rdata.

nodes.name: bytes_to_name_list
nodes.summary: Decodes a DNS wire-format name from a byte buffer into a list of label strings.

nodes.name: end_index_of_name
nodes.summary: Walks a DNS wire buffer to find the byte index immediately after a compressed or uncompressed name, used for SOA record parsing.

nodes.name: txt_data_to_bytes
nodes.summary: Encodes a dict of TXT key-value pairs into DNS TXT record wire format byte sequences.

nodes.name: mdns.py
nodes.summary: Project-level mDNS wrapper providing MDNSResponder — a lifecycle-managed facade around the vendored mdns_client library that handles socket conflicts with the Pico W LWIP built-in mDNS, retry logic, and service advertisement for the ePaper device hostname.
nodes.languageNotes: Detects whether the Pico W LWIP firmware's built-in mDNS is already holding the multicast port and gracefully skips the vendored client in that case; patches socket bind to use INADDR_ANY to avoid dual-binding conflicts.

nodes.name: MDNSResponder
nodes.summary: High-level mDNS service manager that wraps Client and Responder with start/stop/restart lifecycle, retry-with-backoff on bind failures, and LWIP conflict detection for the Pico W.

nodes.name: _builtin_mdns_holds_port
nodes.summary: Probes whether the Pico W LWIP firmware's built-in mDNS responder has already bound port 5353 by attempting a test socket bind and checking for EADDRINUSE.

nodes.name: _patch_bind_to_any
nodes.summary: Monkey-patches the mDNS Client's socket initialization to bind on INADDR_ANY (0.0.0.0) instead of the multicast group address, resolving dual-bind conflicts on MicroPython.

nodes.name: ssd1306_setup.py
nodes.summary: Hardware setup helper that initializes an SSD1306 OLED display over either SPI or I2C, returning the display object for use by the Writer library.

nodes.name: setup
nodes.summary: Initializes the SSD1306 display via SPI or I2C based on the use_spi flag, configuring GPIO pins and returning the display instance.

nodes.name: writer.py
nodes.summary: Core font rendering library providing the Writer and CWriter classes for drawing proportional and monospaced fonts onto MicroPython framebuffer-compatible displays, including ePaper.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses MicroPython-specific APIs such as framebuf.FrameBuffer, bytearray_at, and addressof for zero-copy pixel blitting in CWriter.

nodes.name: Writer
nodes.summary: Base text rendering class that manages cursor position, line wrapping, scrolling, and character blitting for any framebuffer-compatible display device.

nodes.name: CWriter
nodes.summary: Color-capable subclass of Writer that supports foreground/background color via a palette, using zero-copy memory views for efficient pixel blitting on color displays.

nodes.name: writer_demo.py
nodes.summary: Demonstration script that initializes the SSD1306 display and uses the Writer class to render sample text lines, illustrating basic Writer usage.

nodes.name: test
nodes.summary: Runs the Writer demo by setting up the display, drawing a dividing line, and printing three text strings via a Writer instance.

nodes.name: writer_gui.py
nodes.summary: GUI widget library built on top of Writer, providing Label, Meter, and LED display widgets plus circle drawing primitives for building simple on-screen interfaces.

nodes.name: _circle
nodes.summary: Internal Bresenham circle algorithm that plots pixels at eight octant-symmetric points for a given center and radius.

nodes.name: fillcircle
nodes.summary: Draws a filled circle by iterating a Bresenham scan and drawing horizontal lines between symmetric points.

nodes.name: DObject
nodes.summary: Abstract base display object that validates widget placement bounds, manages foreground/background color, and provides the common show/value interface for GUI widgets.

nodes.name: Label
nodes.summary: Text label widget that renders a string at a fixed screen position using a Writer instance, supporting optional clipping and color.

nodes.name: Meter
nodes.summary: Vertical bar-graph meter widget that renders a normalized float value as a filled bar with optional numeric label.

nodes.name: LED
nodes.summary: Circular LED indicator widget that draws a filled circle in a configurable color to represent on/off or status states.

nodes.name: writer_tests.py
nodes.summary: Comprehensive test suite for the Writer/CWriter library, covering inverse display, scrolling, upside-down mode, right-justification, multi-font rendering, tab stops, text wrapping, and dual-display operation.

nodes.name: inverse
nodes.summary: Tests inverse (white-on-black) text rendering by printing three strings with clip mode enabled.

nodes.name: scroll
nodes.summary: Tests automatic screen scrolling by printing lines in a loop until the display scrolls, with timed pauses between frames.

nodes.name: usd_scroll
nodes.summary: Tests upside-down scrolling mode via CWriter with an inverted display, verifying scroll behavior in rotated orientation.

nodes.name: usd
nodes.summary: Tests upside-down (inverted) static text rendering using CWriter.

nodes.name: rjust
nodes.summary: Tests right-justification of text by measuring string pixel widths with stringlen and positioning the cursor accordingly.

nodes.name: fonts
nodes.summary: Tests multi-font rendering by creating two Writer instances with different fonts and printing text with each.

nodes.name: tabs
nodes.summary: Tests tab-stop handling by printing tab-delimited strings and verifying column alignment.

nodes.name: usd_tabs
nodes.summary: Tests tab stops in upside-down (inverted) display mode using CWriter.

nodes.name: wrap
nodes.summary: Tests word-wrap behavior by printing a long string that exceeds display width.

nodes.name: dual
nodes.summary: Tests simultaneous rendering to two independent displays using separate Writer instances, updating Label widgets with random values in a loop.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Configuration persistence layer for the ePaper firmware, providing a JSON-backed key/value store with section-based access, batch write coalescing, and convenience helpers for checking WiFi and weather readiness.

nodes.name: ConfigManager
nodes.summary: Manages reading and writing the device configuration JSON file, supporting lazy loading, batch writes via a context manager, sectioned get/set access, and weather-city storage.

nodes.name: _Batch
nodes.summary: Context manager returned by ConfigManager.batch() that defers file writes until the block exits, coalescing multiple set() calls into a single save.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the Python context manager protocol (__enter__/__exit__) to batch-defer JSON flushes on MicroPython where flash writes are expensive.

nodes.name: web_server.py
nodes.summary: Browser-based HTTP configuration UI for the Pico W ePaper device, serving WiFi, time-zone, and weather-settings pages over an asyncio socket server with URL decoding, form parsing, and live WiFi scanning.

nodes.name: _url_decode
nodes.summary: Decodes a percent-encoded URL string (converting %XX hex escapes and '+' to space) for safe extraction of form field values submitted by the browser.

nodes.name: _page
nodes.summary: Renders the outer HTML page shell — doctype, head, nav bar with active-tab highlighting, and embedded CSS — wrapping any inner body content passed by the caller.

nodes.name: _wifi_page
nodes.summary: Generates the WiFi settings page HTML, listing scanned networks in a dropdown with the currently saved SSID pre-selected and including a JavaScript rescan button that fetches /scan without a page reload.

nodes.name: _time_page
nodes.summary: Generates the time/calendar settings page HTML with 12/24-hour radio buttons, week-start day selector, and a timezone offset dropdown populated from a static list of UTC offsets.

nodes.name: _weather_page
nodes.summary: Generates the weather settings page HTML allowing the user to enter an OpenWeather API key, pick a Taiwan city from the preloaded list, and choose Celsius or Fahrenheit display, with optional weather log output.

nodes.name: WebConfigServer
nodes.summary: Async HTTP server that handles all configuration routes (/wifi, /time, /weather, /done, /scan, /log), dispatching GET and POST requests to the appropriate page-rendering functions and persisting form submissions via ConfigManager.

nodes.name: wifi_manager.py
nodes.summary: WiFi connection manager for the Pico W, handling AP mode (captive-portal hosting), STA mode (connection, reconnection with timeout), RSSI-to-signal-level conversion, and network scanning.

nodes.name: rssi_to_level
nodes.summary: Converts a raw RSSI dBm value to a discrete signal-strength level (0–4) for display on the ePaper status bar.

nodes.name: WiFiManager
nodes.summary: Manages both AP and STA WLAN interfaces on the Pico W, exposing methods to start/stop the access point, connect/disconnect as a station, query connection status and IP, and scan for nearby networks.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the MicroPython `network` module directly; AP and STA interfaces are independent WLAN objects that can run concurrently on the Pico W CYW43 chip.

nodes.name: taiwan_cities.json

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package initializer for the display screens module, providing the `log_display` debug logging helper and the `make_writer` factory function that wraps the Writer class with pixel-doubling and coordinate patching for the ePaper canvas.

nodes.name: log_display

nodes.name: make_writer

nodes.name: __init__.py

nodes.name: EPD_3in7

nodes.name: clock_big.py

nodes.name: font6.py
nodes.summary: Bitmapped font data module for a compact 6px font, providing packed glyph binary data and the standard Writer-compatible metadata and `get_ch` character accessor.

nodes.name: get_ch

nodes.name: freesans20.py
nodes.summary: Bitmapped font data module for the 20px FreeSans proportional sans-serif font, encoding glyph pixel data and providing the Writer-compatible font interface including `get_ch` for character-level bitmap retrieval.

tour.title: Boot Entry Point
tour.description: When the Pico W powers on, MicroPython automatically executes main.py — there is no OS, no shell, and no user interaction. This file is deliberately minimal: it instantiates the App class and calls its async run loop. Understanding this file answers the first question: how does a microcontroller know what to do when the power switch flips?
tour.languageLesson: MicroPython's asyncio (uasyncio) is a cooperative multitasking runtime — not preemptive threads. All concurrent work must yield with 'await' so that other coroutines get CPU time. On a bare-metal microcontroller there is no OS scheduler to fall back on, so a blocked coroutine freezes everything.

tour.title: Application Controller
tour.description: app.py is the brain of the firmware. It defines the device's lifecycle as a state machine with four distinct phases: AP mode (first-run WiFi setup), STA connection (joining a known network), init (syncing time and weather), and the main run loop. With the highest fan-out in the entire codebase (10 direct imports), this file wires together every subsystem — WiFi, NTP, weather, scheduler, and all display screens. Reading it top-to-bottom reveals the full boot narrative.

tour.title: Configuration Persistence
tour.description: config.py is the most depended-upon module in the project (fan-in of 4: app, weather, wifi_manager, and web_server all import it). It provides a JSON-backed key-value store with section-based access so that WiFi credentials, timezone offset, and weather settings survive power cycles. It also exposes convenience helpers like 'is WiFi configured?' and 'is weather configured?' that drive the state machine in app.py.
tour.languageLesson: On a microcontroller, flash storage is the only persistent medium — there is no disk. MicroPython's json module writes to the filesystem on the Pico's internal flash. Batch write coalescing (collecting multiple changes before a single flush) is important because flash has limited write cycles and each write operation has measurable latency.

tour.title: WiFi & First-Run Setup
tour.description: wifi_manager.py handles the two network modes the Pico W supports: AP (access point) mode, where the device itself becomes a hotspot for first-run configuration, and STA (station) mode, where it connects to an existing network. It also converts raw RSSI values into discrete signal-strength levels used by the display. This file, together with app.py's state machine, is what makes the device self-configuring out of the box.
tour.languageLesson: Embedded devices often use a 'captive portal' pattern for first-run setup: the device starts in AP mode, the user connects to it with a phone or laptop, and a lightweight HTTP server (web_server.py here) serves a configuration form. Once credentials are saved, the device reboots into STA mode. This avoids the need to hardcode secrets into firmware.

tour.title: Weather Location Data
tour.description: taiwan_cities.json is a static dataset of Taiwan city coordinates used by web_server.py to populate the weather location selector. It is the only data file in the project and illustrates a common embedded pattern: bundle reference data as a static asset rather than fetching it at runtime to conserve bandwidth and memory. The city chosen here feeds directly into weather.py's API calls.

tour.title: Time Sync with NTP
tour.description: ntp.py provides the sync() function that contacts an NTP server over UDP, applies a configurable timezone offset (read from config.py), and sets the hardware RTC. This is essential because the Pico W has no battery-backed clock — every boot starts at epoch zero. Accurate time is a prerequisite for the scheduler, the calendar display, and timestamped weather logs.
tour.languageLesson: NTP (Network Time Protocol) works by sending a UDP packet to a time server and measuring the round-trip delay. MicroPython's ntptime module handles this, but the hardware RTC must be set manually afterward using machine.RTC().datetime(). Timezone handling is done purely by adding an offset in seconds — there is no timezone database on a microcontroller.

tour.title: Event Scheduler
tour.description: scheduler.py is the heartbeat of the running firmware. It reads the hardware RTC every second and fires named async events — 'minute', 'hour', 'day', 'weather-tick', 'ntp-tick' — at the appropriate intervals. app.py subscribes to these events to trigger display refreshes, weather fetches, and NTP re-syncs. This event-driven design keeps all subsystems decoupled: the scheduler knows nothing about weather or display logic.
tour.languageLesson: This is an observer pattern implemented with async callbacks in MicroPython. Rather than each subsystem having its own polling loop, a single scheduler loop fires events that registered handlers await. This cooperative approach avoids the need for threading and keeps RAM usage predictable — critical on a device with only 264KB of RAM.

tour.title: Weather Fetching
tour.description: weather.py fetches current conditions and forecasts from the OpenWeatherMap API using coordinates provided by the user during setup. It persists responses to a rotating log file so that a stale reading is still available after a network failure. The 'weather-tick' event from scheduler.py triggers periodic fetches, and app.py reads the latest log entry to update the display.

tour.title: ePaper Hardware Driver
tour.description: Pico_ePaper_3_7.py is the lowest-level file in the project. It implements the EPD_3in7 class, communicating with the Waveshare display over SPI and GPIO pins. It supports two rendering modes — 1-bit (black/white, fast) and 4-gray (full quality, slow) — and handles the display's unusual power-up and refresh sequences. Everything in the display layer above depends on this driver, but it knows nothing about the application above it.
tour.languageLesson: ePaper displays use an electrophoretic ink technology: charged particles physically migrate through a fluid when voltage is applied. A full refresh takes 2-4 seconds and produces a characteristic 'flash'. Partial refresh is faster (~0.5s) but only safe for small changed regions — overusing it causes ghosting artifacts. This driver exposes both modes so higher layers can choose the right tradeoff.

tour.title: Canvas Abstraction
tour.description: display/canvas.py sits directly above the hardware driver and is the most imported module in the display layer (fan-in of 6). LandscapeCanvas wraps the EPD framebuffer and handles the coordinate transposition needed because the physical display is wired in portrait orientation but the UI is designed in landscape. It also provides the partial/full refresh API and PBM image blitting, giving all screen renderers a stable drawing surface.

tour.title: Font Rendering Engine
tour.description: writer/writer.py is the vendored Writer/CWriter library — the second most-imported module (fan-in of 4). It renders proportional bitmap fonts onto MicroPython framebuffers by iterating over glyph bitmaps stored in companion font data modules. display/screens/__init__.py's make_writer factory ties Writer to the LandscapeCanvas so that all screens can render text consistently.
tour.languageLesson: MicroPython's framebuf module provides pixel-level drawing but has no text rendering beyond a tiny built-in 8x8 font. The Writer library fills this gap by storing font glyphs as Python byte arrays — no binary file loading needed, which matters because the Pico's filesystem is slow. Fonts are lazy-loaded (display/fonts.py) to avoid importing all glyph data at boot.

tour.title: Main Screen Compositor
tour.description: display/screens/main_screen.py is the primary visual output of the entire project. It composites four information panels onto the canvas: the current time (using the large clock font), today's weather conditions with icons, WiFi signal strength, and a monthly calendar. It uses partial refresh to update only the region of the display that changed — for example, refreshing only the clock area every minute rather than the full screen.

tour.title: Status & Setup Screens
tour.description: The remaining screen renderers handle the device's non-running states. guide.py renders the WiFi AP setup instructions shown during first boot, giving the user the SSID and URL needed to configure the device. message.py renders a centered status text used for transient states like 'Connecting...' or error messages. Together with main_screen.py, these three files cover all visual states the user will encounter.

tour.title: mDNS Network Presence
tour.description: mdns.py wraps the vendored lib/mdns_client library behind a lifecycle-managed MDNSResponder facade. Once connected to WiFi, it advertises the device on the local network under a human-readable name (e.g., pico-epaper.local) so users can access the web configuration UI without knowing the device's IP address. The facade pattern exists because the Pico W's WiFi driver and the mDNS UDP socket have a known conflict that requires careful teardown sequencing.
tour.languageLesson: mDNS (Multicast DNS) allows devices to resolve hostnames like 'device.local' without a DNS server. The device multicasts its own A record answer to the 224.0.0.251 group address. On the Pico W, the CYW43 WiFi chip processes multicast at the hardware level, which can conflict with user-space UDP sockets — hence the need for careful socket lifecycle management in mdns.py.
